description: Future Aerospace Propulsions Corp. (FAPC) is an educational initiative and interactive simulation platform focused on the practical trade-offs of space transport architectures. In modern mission design, the optimal engine is rarely just the most powerful or the most fuel-efficient—it is the one that achieves the mission objectives at the lowest total financial cost.
summary: Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, FAPC’s Rocket Science Simulator is a free Scratch experience created under the fictional company Future Aerospace Propulsions Corp. To make spaceflight easier for everyone to get into, the game throws real-world mission scenarios at you. You have to pick from six different propulsion systems—from standard chemical rockets to photon sails and nuclear engines—to pick the best fit and master aerospace trade-offs.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

FAPC’s Rocket Science Simulator is a scenario-based mission game built in Scratch under the fictional aerospace company Future Aerospace Propulsions Corp. (FAPC). Players act as mission engineers, evaluating real-world spaceflight scenarios—from atmospheric launches to interstellar probes—and selecting the single optimal engine from six systems: Atmospheric Chemical, Vacuum Chemical, Ion, Solar Sail, Photon Sail, and Nuclear Thermal.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

By removing intimidating math and budget spreadsheets, the simulator democratizes aerospace literacy. It gives students and the public an idea on how engineers decide what propulsion type to use next.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Framing the game as a public STEM outreach simulator by FAPC turns a traditional quiz into immersive mission training. Scenarios were designed around real thrust-to-weight, specific impulse, propellant mass, and environmental trade-offs sourced from NASA, ESA, and JAXA research, while keeping the interface beginner-friendly.

Tools & Hardware Used:

Built solo on a personal laptop using Scratch, made by MIT.
